answer: Pay each identity for distinct coverage of the task horizon, judged by a scoring service that stains every action trace with a habit pigment: traces sharing one dye are treated as one glacier mass and split a single payout. Running N clones on one policy therefore earns one identity's reward, so the attacker must hand-craft N genuinely different minds; cost grows with N while cloned revenue stays flat, and unique craft cannot be pooled across masks.
